# Erdős Problem 773

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/773](https://www.erdosproblems.com/773)
- [AlEr85] Alon, Noga and Erdős, P., *An application of graph theory to additive number theory*.
  European J. Combin. (1985), 201-203.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [LeTh95] Lefmann, Hanno and Thiele, Torsten, *Point sets with distinct distances*. Combinatorica
  (1995), 379--408.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos773

open Filter

/--
What is the size of the largest Sidon subset $A\subseteq\{1,2^2,\ldots,N^2\}$? Is it $N^{1-o(1)}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_773 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) ≤
        (Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard
          (Finset.image (fun n : ℕ => n ^ 2) (Finset.Icc 1 N)) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos773

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the largest Sidon subset has size N^{1-o(1)}. Lean gives only the eventual lower bounds N^{1−ε} ≤ M(N) for every ε > 0, without explicitly stating an upper bound or introducing a little-o function.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For N ≥ 1, the extremal cardinality satisfies 1 ≤ M(N) ≤ N: a singleton is Sidon, and the ambient set has at most N elements. Consequently the Lean lower bounds are equivalent to log M(N)/log N tending to 1, precisely the growth statement M(N)=N^{1-o(1)}. The scratch file proves this biconditional, the required cardinality bounds, and the equivalence between the maximum-cardinality bound and existence of a Sidon subset of the required size.

reformulations.difference: Alon–Erdős define B₂ sets using sums of two distinct elements; Lefmann–Thiele's preprint §6 uses the same convention. Lean's IsSidon also considers repeated summands, thus additionally excluding nonconstant three-term arithmetic progressions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This difference does not change the asymptotic question. Theorem 3 of Alon–Erdős, with k=1, partitions any weak B₂ set into at most four subsets containing no nonconstant three-term arithmetic progression. Each part is Sidon in Lean's stronger sense. Thus the two extremal cardinalities satisfy M_strong ≤ M_weak ≤ 4 M_strong. Applying a lower bound with ε/2 and absorbing the factor 4 for sufficiently large N establishes equivalence of their N^{1-o(1)} assertions.
